summary.headline: JSW Cement Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 33% YoY to INR1,912 crore, but operating EBITDA grew only 4% to INR278 crore as cement realisation fell 3% QoQ.
summary.overview: Total volume rose 26% YoY to 3.93 million tons and Nagaur (North) reached EBITDA breakeven in Q2, with a slightly positive contribution. Cement realisation was INR4,781/ton (up 3% YoY, down 3% QoQ), which management attributed mainly to geographic mix, with East volumes up about 20% YoY. Management said cement prices rose in September and October, with non-trade up INR10-30/bag and trade up only in East, and that fuel costs will rise from INR1.84 to about INR2.10 per MCal. Net debt was INR4,287 crore (3.2x net debt/EBITDA), and management reiterated the FY27 capex of about INR2,200-2,300 crore.

segments.name: Cement
segments.commentary: Volume 2.29 million MT, up nearly 40% YoY (about 13% ex-North). Realisation INR4,781/ton, up 3% YoY and down 3% QoQ; trade mix stable at 52%; clinker-to-cement factor 58%.

segments.name: GGBS
segments.commentary: Volume up 7% YoY (Q1 was 2.3%). Realisation INR3,749/ton; no price hike taken, with management prioritising penetration.

segments.name: North (Nagaur)
segments.commentary: Utilisation rose to 75%; EBITDA breakeven in Q2 with slightly positive contribution (about INR3 crore profit). Target EBITDA of INR650-700 crore per ton-equivalent in Q4 per management, with cement sales about 581,000 tons in Q2 including clinker.

segments.name: RMC
segments.commentary: Q2 RMC revenue about INR170 crore; management said margins are minimal as the unit is still ramping up.

guidance_outlook: FY27 cement volume growth guided at high-teens percent over last year.
FY27 GGBS volume growth guided at high-single digits; FY28 also expected at high-single digits.
North cost expected to fall INR550-600/ton from OLBC, WHRS and AFR; North EBITDA expected at about INR700/ton in Q4 FY27.
Fuel cost expected to rise from INR1.84 to about INR2.10/MCal (about INR90/ton on cement cost), offset by green power rising from 41% to above 50%, and price hikes.
Net debt/EBITDA to stay around 3x for about a year, then below 3x.
Capex for FY27 and FY28 of INR2,300 crore and INR2,000 crore reiterated; about INR7,500 crore remains to reach 43.5 MTPA.
Nagaur 2.5 MTPA expansion ready Q4 FY28; Fujairah 1.7 MTPA by Q1 FY28; Dolvi 2 MTPA by about FY29; Vijayanagar 1.5 years from December 2026 start.
capex_capacity: Nagaur WHRS, AFR co-processing and 1 MTPA additional grinding (total about 3.5 MTPA grinding) and OLBC commissioned in Q2 and October 2026.
Added 36 MW wind capacity at Nandyal and Vijayanagar in Q2; green power share 41%.
Nagaur clinker line 3.3 MTPA vs grinding 3.5 MTPA; management expects 2.2-2.3 MTPA of grinding to suffice for current volumes.
Dolvi 2 MTPA grinding on JSW Steel land (lease premium only), work starting January 2027, completion in about 20-21 months.
Further 2 MTPA at Dolvi awaits PNP Jetty land; Vijayanagar expansion starts December 2026. Second GGBS phase to start once utilisation reaches 65-70%.
demand_pricing: October prices (non-trade): South INR15-20/bag, East INR25-30/bag, West INR10/bag, North about INR20/bag; trade up INR10-15/bag only in East so far.
Management said October demand was fairly positive across cement and GGBS; East volumes up about 20% YoY and South about 13%.
Realisation fell 3% QoQ due to geographic mix, not aggressive price cuts, per management.
Lead distance up 9 km QoQ to 294 km.
GGBS priced stable; management says arbitrage vs OPC may be revisited if significant. GGBS penetration in concrete at 35-40%, targeting 50%.
Drought concerns in Karnataka and Andhra: management said not yet affecting its catchment.

qa_highlights.question: Why is cement realisation down 3% QoQ, more than peers, and does the mix hit EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the drop reflects geographic footprint, with no aggressive price cuts. Mix effect flows through to EBITDA, which is already in reported numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did leverage and interest cost rise QoQ while capex run-rate is not higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited land acquisition, use of IPO proceeds, a small extra debt drawdown, and FX loss from unhedged foreign debt after dollar appreciation. Average cost of debt was stable at 7.67%.

qa_highlights.question: Nagaur cost trajectory and fuel cost outlook for Q3-Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost to fall INR550-600/ton with OLBC, WHRS and AFR. Fuel cost to move from INR1.84 to about INR2.10/MCal; fuel stock covers till December or early January. Pet coke spot is INR3.08-3.17.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2 MTPA Dolvi expansion covered by existing land, and when do further expansions start?
qa_highlights.answer: Dolvi 2 MTPA uses JSW Steel-cleared land at the existing site. Balance 2 MTPA awaits PNP Jetty land. Vijayanagar 1.5 years to commissioning from December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How are Nagaur EBITDA and cost guided for Q4, and is there incentive recognition?
qa_highlights.answer: North EBITDA about INR700/ton in Q4. Nagaur INR650 crore 10-year incentive will be recognised once the RIPS entitlement certificate is received, expected around next month.

qa_highlights.question: Why are trade payables around 80 days and when will they fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said payables reflect growth-phase capex and will fall once Rajasthan cash generation starts, around Q4 FY27 end or Q1 FY28.

risks_watch: Fuel cost rise (pet coke at INR3.08-3.17/kcal spot) could pressure Q4 margins if price hikes do not hold; trade price hikes so far only in East.
Net debt/EBITDA at 3.2x and FX loss on unhedged foreign debt; MCLR increases may lift finance cost.
Payables at about 80 days with acceptances; deferred capex payments may slip into April.
Nagaur ramp-up to 2.5 MTPA and EBITDA target of about INR700/ton in Q4 is a key execution test.
RMC margins minimal; management declined to guide FY27 RMC revenue.
Drought and monsoon impact on Karnataka and Andhra demand.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand recovery and price hikes, and on Nagaur's cost reset, but cautious on fuel costs and leverage. Management was evasive on RMC full-year revenue and on the exact East trade-versus-non-trade price gap.
key_quotes: We have not taken any aggressive price cuts if that's what you were alluding to because of which the volume increase has happened.
Happy to announce that at Nagaur, we have achieved EBITDA breakeven in quarter 2.
we have a mandate to keep the net debt to EBITDA below 3.

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 cement volume growth of high-teens % and GGBS high-single digits, backed by commissioned Nagaur grinding (~3.5 MTPA), North utilisation at 75%, and a 2.5 MTPA Nagaur expansion due Q4 FY28; the brief gives no firm FY27 revenue percentage, and pricing fell 3% QoQ.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Nagaur EBITDA targeted at INR650-700/ton in Q4 and cost down INR550-600/ton, but fuel rises from INR1.84 to about INR2.10/MCal (about INR90/ton), partly offset by green power rising from 41% to above 50%; consolidated EBITDA/ton was INR708 in Q2.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Nagaur OLBC, WHRS, AFR and 1 MTPA extra grinding (about 3.5 MTPA total) were commissioned in Q2 and October 2026, Nagaur 2.5 MTPA is due Q4 FY28 (under construction) and Fujairah 1.7 MTPA by Q1 FY28, with total grinding moving from about 3.5 MTPA to the 43.5 MTPA target.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management held FY27 cement volume growth at high-teens % (Q2 volume 3.93 MT, up 26% YoY) and GGBS at high-single digits, with East volumes up about 20% YoY and October demand described as fairly positive.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of INR2,300 crore in FY27 and INR2,000 crore in FY28 reiterated with about INR7,500 crore left to reach 43.5 MTPA, and Dolvi 2 MTPA work starts January 2027, the 2 MTPA balance awaits PNP Jetty land, and Vijayanagar expansion starts December 2026.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held volume guidance and said October non-trade prices rose INR10-30/bag, but trade price hikes so far only in East and fuel cost headwinds limit scope for a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Nagaur must reach INR650-700/ton EBITDA in Q4 from breakeven in Q2, pet coke spot is INR3.08-3.17 and fuel cost is rising to about INR2.10/MCal, with net debt/EBITDA at 3.2x and FX loss on unhedged debt.

rows.label: Nagaur cost reset INR550-600/ton via OLBC, WHRS and AFR
rows.why: Nagaur cost expected to fall INR550-600/ton from OLBC, WHRS and AFR, and Nagaur was at about INR3 crore profit contribution in Q2 with utilisation at 75%.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA to fall below 3x after about a year
rows.why: Net debt at INR4,287 crore is 3.2x EBITDA, management said it stays around 3x for about a year then goes below 3x, with payables around 80 days expected to fall once Rajasthan cash generation starts around Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.

rows.label: Trade payables reduction from about 80 days
rows.why: Payables at about 80 days are tied to growth-phase capex and expected to fall once Rajasthan cash generation starts, with deferred capex payments possibly slipping into April.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, October price hikes and the Nagaur cost reset, but cautious on fuel costs, leverage and payables, and evasive on RMC full-year revenue and the East trade-vs-non-trade price gap; analysts pushed on the 3% QoQ realisation drop, rising leverage and FX loss, and Nagau
